newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MERSON SPURS ARSENAL TO THREE-POINT LEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MERSON SPURS ARSENAL TO THREE-POINT LEAD.

text.p: Midfielder Paul Merson seized the first goal and contributed to the second to spur Arsenal to a 3-1 English premier league win over Southampton on Wednesday, putting the London team three points clear at the top.

Merson grabbed the first goal, his seventh of the season, with a brilliant strike following a free kick just two minutes before halftime, and was brought down by Norwegian defender Claus Lundekvam to provide Ian Wright with a 57th minute goal from the penalty spot.

By then Arsenal had shrugged off the lethargy that inhibited their football in the first 25 minutes, though it surfaced again eight minutes from time when Israeli Eyal Berkovic reduced the deficit with a close-range goal.
However, substitute Paul Shaw sealed the home victory in the final moments of the game with a fine strike for his first-ever Arsenal goal.
The Londoners have 34 points, with second-placed Liverpool, who have a game in hand, on 31.
Dwight Yorke hit his ninth goal in 10 games to lift Aston Villa into fifth place on 27 points after a 2-0 win at West Ham.
Villa outclassed the home side but looked as though they were going to be reliant on a first-half headed goal by Ugo Ehiogu.
However, when West Ham lost concentration at an Andy Townsend corner 16 minutes from time, Yorke took grateful advantage, peeling away from his marker to nod past goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko.
